title: Chapter 9. Travels through the Land
html:
Virachandra in Rarh; the initiation of Gati-Govinda and the story of his birth; Vana-Vishnupur: Parameshvara Dasa Mallik, Srinivasa Acharya and King Vira Hambira; Vishnupur named "Gupta Vrindavana" (pp. 66–78)

[p. 66]

1Glory, glory to Nityananda, Lord of Aja, Bhava and the rest!1
Glory to Mahaprabhu Vira, the ocean of mercy!

2"O Prabhu, moon of Nityananda, sole refuge […],
by whose will even a wretch attains Uttamashloka."2

3O mind, call out: "Nitai-Chaitanya!"
Such merciful Lords you will never find again —
keep them in the lotus of your heart.

4How sweet their play, their dancing and the art of kirtana!
A most profound descent.3
Their own hidden treasure they brought into the mortal world, bestowed it,
and delivered all three worlds.

5The virtue of the touchstone seems trifling to my mind:
it only turns iron to gold at a touch.
But singing the virtues of Nitai and Chaitanya, how many people
have become jewels — in every home!

6Joyfully calling "Hari," performing nama-sankirtana,
they delivered the three worlds.4
Untouchables and pandits alike, singing without pause,
cross the existence of the Kali age with ease.

7"Glory to Nityananda-Rama! The Name — Sri Krishna Chaitanya!" —
crying so, they fall, reeling with the taste of prema.
Says Vrindavana Dasa: in my heart only hope remains —
I, the luckless one, have been left out.

8Glory, glory to Nityananda, glory to the Merciful One,
by merely uttering whose name every perfection is attained!

9Yet in such a name I, a sinner, had no faith,
and my mind did not let go of craving for sense objects and worldly life.

10What shall I do, where shall I go? My mind is not steady
and does not dwell on the virtues of Nitai and Chaitanya.

11This time have mercy, Nitai-Chaitanya:
let my mouth speak nothing but your name,

12let my ears hear nothing but your play and virtues,5
let my eyes see nothing but your form,

13let my hands serve you, O Lord,
and let my mind give no thought to the poison of sense objects.

14May my mind always rest at your holy feet —
grant me this mercy, Prabhu, be kind.

15Now hear of the play and virtues of Virachandra Prabhu:
by hearing them you will be fulfilled, and your burning will abate.

16Virachandra came to Rarh;6
as soon as they heard, the whole land broke out and streamed to him.

17Whoever saw him once kept him ever awake in the heart;
crying "Prabhu has come!", everyone went.

18Some brought curd, milk, coconuts and bananas,
some cloth, some jewels, some flower garlands.

19Coming, they fell at Prabhu's feet saying "Krishna, Krishna!",
and Prabhu, raising both arms, bestowed his mercy:

20"All of you, say 'Krishna, Hari' and go to your homes.
May Gaura-Vishvambhara be merciful to you all!"

21Hearing the blessing, everyone was happy
and gazed their fill at Prabhu's beautiful face.

[p. 67]

22Seeing Kundala,7 Mahaprabhu Vira
cried "Ha, ha, Nityananda!" and was overwhelmed:

23"Where have you gone, O Prabhu, leaving me?
Ha, Krishna Chaitanya!" — and, reeling, he fell.

24Seeing these transformations of prema, all the devotees
began sankirtana, calling "Nitai-Chaitanya!"

25"Glory to Nityananda! Glory, glory to Gaurahari!" —
that sound quickly reached his ears.

26Virachandra rose with a mighty roar,
crying "Nityananda, Nityananda, Chaitanya!"

27In the midst of the sankirtana Vira Raya dances,
and all around the devotees sing the virtues of Hari.

28Thus for a while the sankirtana went on,
and then Prabhu, together with the devotees, brought the kirtana to a close.

29By sankirtana he delivered all the people
and taught everyone: "Always say 'Krishna, Hari.'"

30Seeing Prabhu's mercy, all the people of Rarh
called out without pause: "Nityananda, Gaurachandra!"

31Seeing and hearing this, Prabhu, greatly pleased,
said: "I shall go along the bank of the Ganga."

32"As you command," said all, and set out on the road:
whatever Prabhu wishes is what everyone desires.

33Prabhu rode swiftly on horseback,
and servants with staffs in hand ran ahead.

34On the way he saw Gati coming —
lame in one foot, he came riding in a palanquin.8

35Seeing Prabhu on the road, he had the palanquin set down
and, from a distance, fell prostrate.

36Prabhu on horseback quickly came near
and, still mounted, struck him three times with his whip:

37"Taking Sri Raghunandana for a shudra,9
you are going back home without receiving initiation!"

38Hearing this, Gati was astonished
and fell prostrate at his feet again and again.

39He thought to himself: "Prabhu is the Inner Witness:
what is in my mind he knows in his heart."

40[…] in fear,10 clasping both of Prabhu's feet,
Gati said:

41"Since in punishing me you have shown mercy,
instruct me in the mantra and save my life."

42Prabhu, pleased, took him by the hand
and passed his lotus hand over his head.

43At once, giving him the mantra, he made him his own.
Gati said: "Birth after birth you are my lord."

44Streams of prema flowed from his eyes down his chest;
raising both arms he cried: "I have found it, I have found it!"

45Afterwards all the Vaishnavas came and joined them,
and all sat down under a banyan tree.

46They asked: "Who is this worthy gentleman?"
And Prabhu introduced him in detail:

47"When I was travelling in the South,
in that country I met Srinivasa.11

[p. 68]

48He is a disciple of Gopala Bhatta, foremost among Vaishnavas,
with undivided devotion to the feet of Nityananda and Chaitanya.

49In the land of Tailanga,12 in a brahmana's house,
we stayed together three days in talk of Krishna.

50In the course of it I asked about his circumstances,
and he told me everything about himself from beginning to end:

51'I am the son of Chaitanya Dasa; my home is in Jajigram,
[and my refuge was] with Sarkara Thakura of Srikhanda.13

52He spoke to me about initiation,
and, pleased to hear it, I agreed.

53But at the words of wicked brahmanas my mind turned back —
what could I say to the Thakura? Great was my shame.

54"Being a brahmana, you will become a shudra's disciple!" —
hearing this, my mind was shaken.

55At once I got up and fled,
and, visiting holy places on the way, I reached Vrindavana.

56Sri Gopala Bhatta Gosai showed me mercy:14
he gave me the mantra, gave me books and sent me to Gauda.

57Now I live according to the householder order
and am engaged solely in serving the Vaishnavas.

58Having made a vow, I now feel fear in my mind:
there is no son to carry on the service.

59Give me a son — lame, blind, whatever he be —
and I shall establish him to perform the service.'

[p. 69]

60I said: 'You will certainly have a son.
Bring your wife before me.'

61Then his wife came and bowed to me,
and I told her: 'Take this chewed betel.'

62With great devotion she held out her hand,
and I placed the betel from my lips in her hand.15

63Deeming herself blessed, she ate that nectar of the lips,
and by my grace she conceived soon after.

64From that was born this son of his —
a vessel of my favour, I tell you plainly."

65Hearing this, all the Vaishnavas rejoiced
and said: "He is worthy of honour."

66Gati, clasping the Gosai's feet, said:
"Prabhu, you have come to this land out of mercy.

67I dare not say it, yet my heart desires:
may your holy feet visit my home."

68Subject to his devotees, he accepted the devotee's words
and told him: "I will come."

69That day he stayed in the house of some fortunate man,
and thus all, through one another, were fulfilled.

70On the way to Vanabhumi16 there were great festivals in village after village,
and so many people became true Vaishnavas!

71Prabhu taught everyone the dharma of sankirtana:
"In the Kali age there is no other dharma or duty.

72Worship Krishna, remember Krishna, take the name of Krishna —
by this, truly, truly, you will reach Krishna's abode.

73Regard all alike, serve guests —
this is the householder's dharma; practise it always."

74Receiving Prabhu's teaching, the fortunate people
take the name of Krishna and serve guests.

75Virachandra entered Vanabhumi
and, seeing a lovely place, rejoiced in his heart.

76Seeing the clear river water and the solitude,
he said: "Here I shall perform my bath."

77Leaving his conveyance, he sat beneath a mango tree,
and at once the horn sounded and [the banner went up] for a halt.

78Across the river, close by, lived a worthy gentleman
named Parameshvara Dasa Mallik.17

79He and his whole family were of Nityananda's company;
hearing [the news], he came, greatly delighted.

80He fell prostrate at Prabhu's feet
and, clasping them, wept, crying "Nityananda!"

81"My father Nityananda, the life of the fallen,
delivered even a fallen one like me.

82I never again saw that moon-like face,
and my sinful life goes on without Prabhu."

83Saying this, he wept, holding Prabhu's holy feet:
"Virachandra, O father, I take refuge in you!

84You are Nityananda, you are Shachi's son,
you are Krishna, you are Vishnu, the essence of the world.

85Showing yourself to one such as me,18
you have fulfilled me once more, melting with mercy."

86So Mallik wept, unsteady in prema.
Seeing this, Virachandra Mahashaya was amazed.

87Knowing him to be a recipient of Prabhu's mercy, he was filled with prema
and began to weep, crying "Ha, ha, Nityananda!"

88With mercy glancing kindly with his lotus eyes,
he raised him up and embraced him with love.

89Then Mallik poured out his entreaty
and with great eagerness took him to his own house.

[p. 70]

90With devotion he and his whole family fell at the holy feet,
and seated him on a splendid seat in the main house.

91Washing the holy feet, he took the charanamrita,19
and, after he and his family drank it, sprinkled it about the house.

92Seeing him as his own servant, Prabhu showed him such mercy:
Mallik obtained a grace hard even for Brahma to obtain.

93He asked Gati: "Where did you become his companion?"
And Gati began to tell all that had happened to him.

94Hearing it, Mallik was very pleased
and from that day loved him more than life.

95All the Vaishnava associates he honoured,
washed their feet, bowed and seated them.

96All bustled eagerly to serve Prabhu,
and each joyfully prepared something.

97One brought cool water and scented it,
another anointed Prabhu's body with fragrant vishnu-taila.

98Some brought flowers, some ground sandalwood,
some made a casket of new cloth.

99Some strung fragrant garlands,
some prepared a bed of tulasi.

100Someone decorated a place for the worship
and set a splendid seat upon it.

101Having prepared the articles for worship with sixteen offerings,
he stands with all his household, cloth draped about his neck.20

102Prabhu performed his bath on a low stool
and, as was his daily custom, performed the worship of Vishnu.

103Mallik's household offered worship:
with sixteen offerings they worshipped Prabhu's feet.

104They performed arati, waving lamps in many ways,
and the devotees began kirtana.

105For a long time there was sankirtana, dancing and singing;
then, closing the kirtana briefly, all rested.

106With great reverence and devotion Prabhu drank water,
and the remainder was shared among all the Vaishnavas.

107Many provisions were prepared for cooking,
and the cook was respectfully led inside.

108How many kinds of vegetable dishes and soups he made!
Shali rice and wheat breads — in heaps.

109Prabhu sits on a splendid bedstead,
and nearby the Vaishnavas converse about their beloved Lord.

110At his feet sits Gati-Govinda
and, with great joy in his heart, serves his feet.

111He asks Prabhu about the true nature of things:
"How can a living being cross over worldly existence?"

112Mercifully Prabhu expounded the whole truth:
the meaning of aishvarya and madhurya, prema and bhakti,

113taking shelter at the guru's feet, the ninefold practice of bhakti,
the marks of bhakti — hearing, chanting and the rest,

114the eternal play of Radha and Krishna with its many varieties of rasa,
and the other hidden play that even the Vedas do not know.

115"Following Ananga Manjari, [sister] of Radha,21
understanding the glance of the sakhi whose mood you have taken shelter in,

116render loving service, discerning the right moment,
enraptured by beauty and virtue, sheltered in that mood.

117Always cherish attachment to Krishna's name and virtues,
and know the son of Vraja's king as the lord of your life.

118Vrishabhanu's daughter, who enchants Govinda —
service to her day and night,

119always abiding by her side as her companion —
thus is ragatmika bhajana practised."22

120All this truth he revealed to Gati-Govinda,
and finally gave him a firm command:

[p. 71]

121"In the Kali age the goal is Chaitanya and Nitai alone;
without the practice of Hari-nama there is no other way.

122In the company of Krishna's devotees take the name of Krishna —
truly, truly, truly, you will reach the abode of Radha and Krishna.

123Be always careful with Vaishnavas:
if you offend a Vaishnava there is no deliverance."

124Placing his own lotus foot on his head,
he blessed him: "May all this be revealed to you."

125Once more he said mercifully:
"Casting far away pride and conceit,

126with respect for all beings and a humble nature —
only then will you gain true love for Krishna."

127Receiving the command from the holy lips, Sri Gati-Govinda
was filled with prema, his whole body blissful.

128Clasping his feet, he wept, giving himself over:
"May I never forget these lotus feet!"

129At that moment Sri Krishna's offering was removed,
and conches and bells began to sound for arati.

130Having made the offering, they called Prabhu;
Prabhu partook of prasada and rinsed his mouth.

131Everyone received the remnants of the prasada —
thus in joy and gladness the day passed.

132At night he holds kirtana with great bliss —
not even Ananta himself could describe it.

133How Virachandra manifested in the kirtana circle,
in what mood and what form — Vyasa alone knows.

134Some see him with crest and dhoti, of pauganda age,23
some see him entering fresh youth.

135Some see him white-hued, with plough and club,24
some see him as Shyamasundara with flute in hand.

136Some see him as Madana-mohana, king of rasa,
some dancing in the kirtana assembly in a sannyasi's dress.

137"Say Hari, say Hari!" he cries, raising both arms,
and with his tears bathes the bodies of all the devotees.

138Some see him four-armed, with conch and disc in his hands,
and Sri Ananta holding an umbrella over him with a thousand heads.

139Spreading a net of rays of compassion in all directions,
he draws people in — devotees and non-devotees alike.

140As at the beginning of the rasa dance Krishna with the song of his flute
drew all the gopis to him,

141so he drew [people] by kirtana,
and all came to watch the kirtana.

142Seeing that bliss and that kirtana, all the people
floated in love for Krishna, saying "Krishna" with their lips.

143Srinivasa Acharya, with the Vaishnavas,
was sitting rapt in prema, delighting in talk of Krishna.

144At that moment the sweet sound of kirtana came
and touched his ears — and he became as one mad.

145"How sweet!" he cried and ran off quickly,
and all the Vaishnavas there ran after him.

146Arriving quickly, they joined the kirtana circle
and all at once beheld the manifestation of Virachandra.

147Gentle, calm, grave Pandita Srinivasa,
at the sight of Virachandra, was overwhelmed.

148Mallik, standing by Prabhu's side, was shedding tears:
from the nectar of seeing Prabhu his eyes simply streamed.

149Seeing the Acharya's arrival at the kirtana,
he began to speak, looking at Prabhu's face.

150Mallik said: "Here comes Srinivasa."
Seeing him, Prabhu's heart greatly rejoiced.

151Spreading his arms, he embraced him,
and Srinivasa offered him many kinds of praise.

[p. 72]

152Falling at his feet, he rolled in the dust of his feet,
saying: "Grace! Supreme bliss!"

153In the midst of the kirtana he dances, raising both arms,
crying "Virachandra! Nityananda! Gauranga!"

154At Prabhu's beauty and the bliss of the kirtana
Srinivasa, full of prema and joy, was amazed.

155Crying "Blessed, blessed!", all the people floated in prema,
seeing the manifestation of Mahaprabhu Virachandra.

156Some say: "I shall never be born again,"
some: "In the Kali age I see Prabhu face to face."

157Some say: "We have overcome Yama's power:
such a Prabhu walks visibly among all beings."

158What a Prabhu, what companions, what a sankirtana! —
seeing and hearing it, all the people were delivered.

159Thus in the bliss of kirtana much of the night passed.
Prabhu understood in his heart that the kirtana singers were weary,

160and said: "Today pause the kirtana;
calm yourselves, sit down and take the name of Krishna."

161Saying "Hari, Hari," all closed the kirtana,
yet for four dandas25 its echo stayed in their ears.

162At night two dandas passed in the bliss of the meal,
and another two dandas in talk of worldly matters.

163At last, late in the night, Prabhu fell asleep
and rose at dawn saying "Krishna Chaitanya!"

164The Vaishnavas performed mangala-arati,
and all, having done their morning duties, came.

165Gati asks that Prabhu's holy feet proceed [to his home]
and stands in front together with Srinivasa.

166Prabhu told the Acharya Gati's story,
and, hearing it, the Acharya was overjoyed.

167With much entreaty he speaks at Prabhu's feet:
"I, my household, my sons and all my friends —

168we have no refuge but these lotus feet.
You are a second body, the very form of Chaitanya."

169Thus the Acharya offered many praises,
and, hearing them, Virachandra Prabhu was pleased.

170Smiling slightly, Prabhu said:
"There is no difference between you and me."

171Mallik came and worshipped Prabhu's feet,
and all, children and elders, came and prostrated themselves.

172Raising his foot, he placed it on everyone's head,
saying: "May Nitai-Chaitanya be merciful."

173Mounting his conveyance, Prabhu proceeds in his play,
and ahead go the Vaishnavas performing kirtana.

174At Prabhu's sign the Vaishnavas
perform kirtana, calling "Nitai-Chaitanya!"

175"Just once, O mind, say 'Nitai-Chaitanya!'"
[…]26

176Hearing the kirtana, Prabhu smiles gently,
and Premananda Dasa27 roars and dances.

177The Acharya's son28 hurried on ahead
and arranged many kinds of articles for worship.

178From far off he spread clean cloths
along the road by which [Prabhu] was coming with kirtana.

179Preparing the worship with sixteen offerings,
he set everything out in its proper place.

180Near the house rose the sound of kirtana,
and hearing it, the people, amazed, came out at once.

181Gati came forward a little ahead,
and the townsfolk stood on both sides.

182Revealing majesty and sweetness at once,
he amazed everyone and captivated their hearts.

[p. 73]

183All around, all the people cry "Hari, Hari,"
and everyone floats as if on waves of bliss.

184Virachandra dwelt in everyone's body;
the very form of bliss, he gives bliss to all.

185Whoever sees Prabhu cries "Hari, Hari":
seeing his beauty, all gave him their hearts.

186All say: "This is Narayana himself" —
so said everyone, high, middling and the rest.

187The holy feet went into the house,
and [radiance] spread in all directions like lightning.

188The Acharya's family, with all the household —
none could contain in their bodies the joy of seeing him.

189Seeing Prabhu's beauty, the charm of millions of Kandarpas,
everyone was astonished at heart.

190All fall prostrate on the ground,
and on everyone's lips: "Krishna, Krishna, Hari!"

191All say: "This land has become supremely blessed —
such a great being has descended into our land!"

192All say: "We have heard that in the town of Nadia
the Lord himself descended.

193That same Prabhu has manifested again.
Who can know the truth of the Lord and the Lord's play?"

194Sarasvati speaks the truth, though people do not know it:
this is that same Gaura, in person, in the form of Vira.

195In the courtyard all the Vaishnavas perform kirtana,
and Srinivasa dances together with his son.

196Some dance, some sing, some cry "Hari,"
and all the Nadas29 proudly shout "Vira, Vira!"

197Thus the sankirtana went on for some time,
and then at Prabhu's command all brought the kirtana to a close.

198At the end of the kirtana they washed Prabhu's feet,
and the whole family drank [the water] and placed it on their heads.

199"Showing such mercy, you have accepted me;
I am fulfilled," [the Acharya] says again and again.

200With all his household he prepares for the service,
and the Acharya's devotion pleased Prabhu's heart.

201Greeting the Vaishnavas as was fitting,
he seated them with great respect.

202Prabhu with his companions bathed and gave gifts
and, sitting on the bedstead, chants the names by count.

203A brahmana cook began the cooking,
and the Acharya lovingly cooked many dishes himself.

204Thus the cooking was completed;
arranging it in vessels, they offered it to Krishna.

205Prabhu went and partook of that offering
and rinsed his mouth with fine scented water.

206Gati gathered up the remnants of the prasada
and gave a little to each of the Vaishnavas.

207The Acharya with his household received the maha-prasada
and, crying "I am fulfilled!", floated in bliss:

208"Today Sri Krishna Chaitanya is gracious to me;
today my service to the Vaishnavas has borne its fruit.

209Serving Krishna's devotees bears this fruit:
Krishna, pleased, bestows his mercy.

210This is the certain fruit of serving Vaishnavas:
Krishna makes one his own and takes one among his intimates.

211Whatever one's mood, it is perfected without effort:
by the power of serving devotees every perfection is attained."

212Having thus spoken of the glory of the Vaishnavas,
the Acharya remains immersed in the ocean of prema.

213Having thus completed the blissful meal,
at night Prabhu began sweet kirtana.

[p. 74]

214Vira Hambira was the ruler of that land.30
The king sat in his court, as royal custom requires.

215There they spoke among themselves of Prabhu's virtues and his kirtana,
and the king said: "I long to see him.

216But what if he, in disdain, will not see me?
What if he will not accept me, a worldly man?

217Yet Nityananda delivers the fallen,
as the sun's rays reach everywhere.

218Tomorrow morning I shall ask the Thakura
how I may have an audience with Prabhu."

219As he sat thus, talking in eagerness,
the sweet sound of kirtana reached him.

220Who knows how much sweetness is in that kirtana! —
as though a flood of nectar had entered his ears.

221As if a mantra of attraction were at work —
so spread Virachandra's kirtana.

222As once in Vrindavana the son of Nanda
enchanted the hearts of the gopis with the song of his flute,

223and the gopis, as if mad, came to Krishna,
and Krishna enchanted the gopis with the taste of the rasa dance —

224so by the attraction of Virachandra's kirtana
people's hearts were enchanted by the name and virtues of Krishna.

225Like a madman [the king] went, possessed by prema,
crying "Krishna, Krishna," awash in tears.

226The king came and entered the house
and, seeing the [kirtana] circle, was astonished.

227And above all Virachandra, in the midst of the circle:
radiance seems to glitter even outside him.

228Rows of lamps burn on every side,
and their reflection falls upon his holy body.

229His head is wrapped in fine white cloth,
clusters of curling locks lie upon his back.

230Precious elephant pearls swing at his ears,
the corners of his lotus eyes touch his ears.

231Red lips, and behind them the gleam of teeth;
the colour of his body like the morning sun.

232Arms reaching to the knees, a beautiful build —
seeing him, Madana himself forgets his own abode.

233Seeing the movement of his feet, [it seems] that in the guise of moon-like nails
the hosts of Kama have gathered at his lotus feet.31

234His hair stands on end, surpassing kadamba filaments;
now he laughs aloud, now he is stunned motionless.

235Tears pour from his eyes like a raincloud,
and the whole kirtana circle is drenched.

236Taking a fan of peacock feathers in hand,
the Acharya moves close by, fanning him.

237That fan seems to sway within his body —
seeing it, all the people fall to the ground.

238What dazzling splendour — without and within!
Brimming, overflowing with prema, he sports in the kirtana.

239The king watches, his hand resting on a servant's shoulder,
and, unable to stand, sinks to the ground.

240The servants hurriedly caught him and lifted him up,
and the Acharya's son reported it at Prabhu's feet.

241Hearing this, the Saviour of the fallen melted with mercy:
he embraced him and bestowed his holy feet.

242At the mere touch the king was overwhelmed —
Sri Vira Hambira became a full vessel of mercy.

243All around, all the people cry "Hari, Hari,"
and everyone floats on waves of bliss.

244Such is the play of Virachandra Raya —
who could know it if he does not reveal it himself?

[p. 75]

245When the night was ending, the kirtana came to rest,
and the tidings of such bliss spread through the land.

246The king, deeming himself blessed, went to his palace,
and at the end of the night he saw again in a dream:

247in the same guise, with the same kirtana and dancing,
[Prabhu] with his companions entered his house.

248Standing before him, he said with a smile:
"I have come to your land to show you mercy.

249I am pleased to see your devotion;
in your house I have stayed, I have stayed."

250Next he sees him as a sannyasi bearing a kamandalu —
the very form of Chaitanya, softly smiling,

251chanting with holy lips "Hare Krishna, Hare Krishna."
Seeing this, the maharaja was greatly amazed.

252Next he sees him white and dark in colour:
he sees the plough and club — and lips with a flute.

253Looking at the king, he says with a smile:
"Do you know me, King, for certain, in your heart?"

254Saying this, Prabhu vanished,
and the king keeps saying: "What am I seeing? What am I seeing?"

255The sleep broke; the king looks all around —
no one anywhere; the night has turned to morning.

256Having performed his morning duties, the king, eager at heart,
hastily sent for the Acharya.

257His body quivering with prema, his hair on end —
seeing the signs of Krishna's mercy, the Acharya was amazed:

258"What did you see? What happened? Tell me truly."
With tears and trembling the king tells the Acharya.

259The king told the Acharya everything,
and, having heard, the Acharya said to the king:

260"Merciful Sri Virachandra is Chaitanya himself;
he has appeared here to show you mercy.

261He is that same Chaitanya Gosai, descended in secret;
he is merciful to all beings, pouring out compassion.

262Boundless is this glory of Chaitanya Gosai —
there will never be such a merciful Prabhu again."

263Speaking of Chaitanya's virtues, Acharya Thakura,
brimming with prema, cries "Ha Gaura! Ha Gaura!"

264Embracing, the two of them weep
and, crying "Ha Krishna Chaitanya!", roar again and again.

265After a while, both saying "Krishna, Krishna,"
grew calm and embraced once more.

266The Acharya says: "King, you are fulfilled:
you are fortunate — such mercy has been shown you."

267The king asks: "How may I have an audience with Prabhu?"
And he spoke to Prabhu's companions.

268The companions went and told Prabhu,
relating everything about the king's longing.

269Smiling, Prabhu said with his own lips:
"Chaitanya Gosai himself has shown him mercy.

270The king's heart's desire will be fulfilled —
merciful Chaitanya Gosai will surely do it."

271[The Acharya] came to the king and told him Prabhu's merciful words,
and, hearing them, the king rejoiced at heart.

272Bowing to Prabhu's feet, the devotee [king]
took leave of the Acharya and departed.

273Thus Virachandra, in the Acharya's house,
was absorbed day and night in discussing many shastras.

274Every day [people] saw ever new play,
while the king's heart [longed] for him to grace his house.32

275One morning Prabhu rose and went into the forest
and rejoiced to see the forest's beauty.

[p. 76]

276Wandering, he sees a lovely spot —
near the water, a secluded grove.

277His nostrils were delighted by the fragrance of flowers;
as if restless, he looks about in all directions.

278He saw that close by there was a bower,
and all the trees were laden with fruits and roots.

279Cuckoos and bees drink honey,
peacocks and peahens cry and dance.

280In the distance, in the forest, a boy playing the flute
brings the cows to drink.

281Seeing and hearing this, Prabhu, overcome by prema,
reeled and fell to the ground beneath a tree.

282Crying "Krishna, Krishna," Prabhu lost consciousness,
and, seeing this, the Vaishnavas were thrown into confusion.

283The Vaishnavas lifted him and held him to their breasts,
and, surrounding him, sweetly sing Krishna-sankirtana.

284The king heard all these tidings
and lovingly went to see him.

285Eyes closed, cheeks bathed in tears of prema,
hair on end like a palasha tree in bloom.33

286The king looked at his feet,
and all saw the marks of flag, thunderbolt and goad.34

287[…] limbs without visible joints, a tall stature35 —
seeing this, the king was astounded.

288The king — a great devotee, wise, mighty in learning —
sees in Prabhu all the marks of the Lord.

289After a long while Virachandra returned to outward awareness,
and the king, with tearful eyes, [honoured] his lotus feet.

290With cloth draped about his neck he entreats
and says: "Deliver me, Prabhu!

291May your feet grace my house —
then my heart's desire will be fulfilled."

292Prabhu, being pleased with the king,
set off on foot at a quick pace.

293Along the way he sees many temples,
and the joy in his heart toward the king grows still more.

294Prabhu entered the king's palace,
and they seated him in a splendid, charming place.

295The king himself washed his feet
and, gazing on them, was bathed in tears.

296Wiping the holy feet with pure white cloth,
he drank the charanamrita, deeming himself blessed.

297As soon as he drank the holy charanamrita
he floated in love for Krishna, and tears streamed from his eyes.

298All over the king's body the hair stood on end;
seeing the king's devotion, the best of Prabhus was pleased.

299With joy in his heart the king served him in many ways
and wept, crying: "Mahaprabhu Virachandra!

300To deliver me, Prabhu, you came to my house —
the name 'Saviour of the fallen' has resounded in the world.

301You are Krishna himself, the very self of Chaitanya;
to deliver beings you play this play.

302Unless you yourself reveal it, who could know?
You perform hidden play upon the earth, Prabhu.

303Glory, glory to Sri Krishna Chaitanya — Virachandra!
Make me a servant of your feet and cut the bonds of worldly existence."

304So many such praises he offered — who could count them?
Virachandra Prabhu smiles, looking at the king.

305Prabhu says: "King, you are most fortunate:
you are my servant, of this there is no doubt.

306But do not reveal who I am.
Keep this command of mine in your heart."

[p. 77]

307"As you command," said the king, folding his palms,
and Prabhu placed his holy feet upon the king's head.

308Receiving a grace hard even for Brahma to obtain, the king
kept Prabhu's rosy feet in his heart.

309Day after day he serves Prabhu in new ways,
and day by day his love for Prabhu grows.

310Prabhu, viewing the temples day after day,
is inspired and happy at heart.

311Outside, the king holds great festivals,
and the Vaishnavas dance in kirtana without cease.

312At night Prabhu comes and performs kirtana —
sweet, sweet singing and sweet dancing.

313He sings aloud, calling the name of Krishna:
"Krishna, Krishna! Rama, Rama!" — he cries "Hari, Hari!"

314This sound of Krishna's name delivers the beings
into whose ears its echo enters.

315Even the unmoving and the moving were delivered —
such a sankirtana did Mahaprabhu make manifest.

316Blessed, blessed is Mahaprabhu Sri Krishna Chaitanya,
by whose mercy all beings were blessed!

317Sankirtana appeared, revealing bhakti,
and Virachandra himself spread that dharma.

318The whole land was blessed by performing sankirtana:
practising it himself, he taught the people of the world:

319"All of you, sing of Krishna, dance, cry 'Hari, Hari' —
and all will easily cross the fear of worldly existence.

320Remaining in worldly life, set your hope on Krishna's feet;
with wives, sons and kin, become servants of Krishna.

321Householder or renunciant — this is the essence of dharma:
in the Kali age there is none other than this.

322The root dharma of a householder is serving guests;
keeping this dharma, perform Krishna-sankirtana.

323The renunciant, his mind turned away from worldly things,
should restrain the senses, taking the name of Krishna.

324This dharma of the renunciant is very hard:
through talk of worldly things he loses bhakti for Krishna.

325Therefore let the renunciant be careful in this
and never go near worldly people.

326The householder's order is very accessible,
if, living in the world, one is attached to Krishna,

327serves guru, Krishna and the Vaishnavas,
and the mind is in no way attached to worldly things.

328Taking Krishna's name, always full of longing,
one crosses worldly existence, singing Krishna's name.

329This dharma Virachandra spreads in the world:
without Krishna the world has no other way."

330Receiving Prabhu's command, with all his heart,36
with wives, sons, kinsmen and his own people —

331hearing those words, the king accepted them
and brought all his subjects to Krishna-sankirtana.

332As King Yudhishthira, at Vyasa's word,
brought his subjects to it in Hastinapura,37

333so the king spread it in Vana-Vishnupur,
and thus Vishnupur became famed as "Gupta Vrindavana."38

334Such was Prabhu's command to Sri Vira Hambira:
"Bring all your subjects to this dharma."

335As once Nitai and Chaitanya spread it,
in the same way Virachandra Prabhu plays his play.

336Ceaselessly Virachandra, together with the devotees,
delivers beings, ever singing of Krishna.

337The king always stays near Prabhu:
without Prabhu the king's heart is never at rest.

[p. 78]

338The king says: "Prabhu, I will not let you go;
if you leave this place I shall give up my life."

339Ever in that bliss of prema, [he made Vishnupur] a holy abode
and gave Vishnupur the name "Gupta Vrindavana."

340Prabhu says: "Here is my abiding presence;
here there will be kirtana and dancing without end.

341Many more mahantas will come to this place;
there will never be calamity or want of wealth.

342In all your line I shall abide;
with devotion and power [your descendants] will bestow prema.

343But if faith in Nityananda's feet should waver,39
through unbelief all wealth will be ruined."

344Hearing such a boon from Prabhu,
the king at once deemed himself fulfilled.

345With cloth about his neck the king fell at his feet
and wet them with the tears of both his eyes.

346Such a merciful avatara as Virachandra
there has not been, has not been, brothers, nor will there be.

347Leaving such a Prabhu, whom else would one worship?
Merely seeing him, the mind sinks in an ocean of bliss.

348Let each have his own mind — whether he perish or not —
but may my mind remain ever at those feet.

349If someone, seeing and hearing, still feels discontent —
who begs anyone to drink nectar?

350Thus Virachandra in Vana-Vishnupur
ever delights in the rasa of Hari-sankirtana.

351Setting my hope on the feet of Virachandra Prabhu,
Vrindavana Dasa tells the "Vamsha-vistara."

Thus ends the ninth chapter, called "Travels through the Land," in the Antya-lila of the "Nityananda-vamsha-vistara."

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. Aja ("the Unborn") is Brahma; Bhava is Shiva. "Mahaprabhu Vira," "Vira" and "Vira Raya" are names of Virachandra in this chapter.
  2. The Sanskrit verse is badly corrupted in both copies ("aprekṣaika gati nityānanda candramaẏaī prabho, yadicchaẏaā pāmaro'pi uttamaślokamīẏate"); the translation is approximate and the opening of the first line is unclear. Uttamashloka ("praised in the finest verses") is an epithet of Krishna.
  3. A tripadi song (stanzas 3–7). The line "atīva gambhīra avatāra" is taken from copy B (illegible in A); "kari vara dāne" is B's reading.
  4. "tinaloka karila nistāre" is a conjecture; the copies have "nijñāve/nijkāve." "Untouchables and pandits": in A the word "asparśa" stands apart; in B it opens the line.
  5. Line restored from copy B ("līlā guṇa vine karṇa nā śunaẏa"); A has garbage in its place.
  6. Both copies read "jhāṛhae"; the OCR regularly confuses "ra" and "jha," and "the people of Rarh" (rāṛha loka) are named just below, so we read "rāṛhae" — Rarh (Radha-desha), western Bengal west of the Bhagirathi.
  7. "kuṇḍala darśana kari" — "seeing Kundala." Literally "earring"; probably a place associated with Nityananda (seeing it, Virachandra remembers his father), but possibly an earring kept as a relic. The text does not make it clear; the transition across the page break is abrupt.
  8. Gati is Gati-Govinda, son of Srinivasa Acharya (see below, 47–64). A dola is a litter or palanquin.
  9. Raghunandana Thakura of Srikhanda, nephew of Narahari Sarkara, belonged to the vaidya caste, which brahmanas counted as shudra. Virachandra rebukes Gati for the caste prejudice that kept him from taking initiation.
  10. The opening of the line is corrupt ("bhāẏaā gabhūva ganta mune bhaẏa pāiẏaā"); perhaps "jāniẏaā prabhura tattva mane bhaẏa pāiẏaā" — "realizing Prabhu's true nature, afraid at heart."
  11. Virachandra is the narrator; in 50–59 he quotes Srinivasa's words in the first person. Srinivasa Acharya was a disciple of Gopala Bhatta Gosvami and a preacher in Vishnupur.
  12. Tailanga is the Telugu country in South India.
  13. Chaitanya Dasa was Srinivasa's father; Jajigram is his home village. Sarkara Thakura is Narahari Sarkara of Srikhanda. The second line rhymes "vāṛai/vāṛaī" and is unclear; the bracketed words are supplied from context.
  14. Gopala Bhatta Gosvami, one of the Six Gosvamis of Vrindavana.
  15. Chewed betel (adharamrita, "nectar of the lips") — a holy person's remnants given as a blessing.
  16. Vanabhumi is Vana-Vishnupur (Vishnupur), capital of the kingdom of Mallabhum (present-day Bankura district).
  17. Parameshvara Dasa Mallik — a local Vaishnava who, according to the text, belonged to Nityananda's company.
  18. The word before "me" is corrupt ("nivinta/nidhimvā"); rendered by sense.
  19. Charanamrita is the water that has bathed the feet of a holy person or deity; it is drunk and sprinkled as something sacred.
  20. The sixteen offerings (shodashopachara) make up the full rite of worship. Cloth about the neck is a gesture of humility and supplication.
  21. "rādhānaṅgamañjarī" — Ananga Manjari, Radha's younger sister; in Nityananda's tradition Jahnava Devi is held to be her incarnation. Virachandra instructs Gati in service within her following.
  22. So the text ("rāgātmika"); what is described is the practice of raganuga bhakti, following Radha's companions, whose love is ragatmika.
  23. Pauganda is the age from five to ten; the crest (chuda) with a peacock feather and the dhoti (dhada) are the dress of the cowherd Krishna.
  24. The plough and the club are Balarama's emblems.
  25. A danda is a measure of time, about 24 minutes.
  26. The second line of the couplet is illegible in both copies (fragments "ci," "varā").
  27. Premananda Dasa — apparently one of Virachandra's companions; possibly also an epithet ("a servant full of the bliss of prema").
  28. "ācārya nandana" — the Acharya's son, i.e. Gati-Govinda.
  29. Nada (nāṛaā) — shaven-headed mendicants whom, by tradition, Virachandra brought into Vaishnavism (1,200 Nadas and 1,300 Nadis).
  30. Vira Hambira, king of Mallabhum (Vishnupur), a disciple of Srinivasa Acharya. "Deyan" (deẏaāna, diwan) is the royal audience hall or council.
  31. An obscure and corrupt line ("kāẏavuva haẏaā vahe / kāẏavu|va iẏaā i"); the reading "kāmavyūha haiẏaā rahe" is a conjecture.
  32. The second line of the couplet is unclear ("gṛhete darśana dena nṛpatira mana"); rendered by sense in light of the later invitation to the palace.
  33. The palasha (Butea monosperma) is a tree that becomes entirely covered in blossoms; an image of hair standing on end.
  34. Flag, thunderbolt (vajra) and goad are auspicious marks on the feet of God.
  35. The first word of the line is illegible ("śrae/maṇa").
  36. The line is unclear ("pāiẏaā prabhura ājñā sava haẏa mana"); its subject seems to be the king of the following couplet.
  37. Yudhishthira, eldest of the Pandavas, king of Hastinapura; Vyasa, compiler of the Mahabharata.
  38. Gupta Vrindavana, "the Hidden Vrindavana," is the traditional epithet of Vishnupur.
  39. The copies read "ncale/nañcile"; read by sense as "should waver" (na cale / ṭalile).
